title: Taiwan delegation attends 25th Berlin Security Conference, showcasing nation’s capabilities in diplomacy, defense, and whole-of-society resilience
text:
The 25th Berlin Security Conference (BSC) was held in Berlin, Germany, from November 3 to 4. Minister of Foreign Affairs Lin Chia-lung was invited to deliver a prerecorded speech at the event. In addition, Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs François Chihchung Wu, Deputy Secretary-General of the National Security Council Lin Fei-fan, and Lieutenant General Hsieh Jih-sheng, Deputy Chief of the General Staff for Intelligence of the Ministry of National Defense, were also invited to participate in an interview in the afternoon of November 4.

In his prerecorded video address on November 4, Minister Lin noted that the security and prosperity of Taiwan and Europe were increasingly interconnected. He said that Taiwan was a critical hub for the global semiconductor, AI, ICT, and advanced manufacturing industries and that Taiwan and Europe could further deepen cooperation in semiconductors, AI, critical infrastructure, cybersecurity, energy security, and other strategic domains.

Furthermore, Minister Lin emphasized that Taiwan had long faced gray-zone activities, foreign information manipulation, and other hybrid threats and had accumulated practical experience in promoting whole-of-society resilience. This could serve as a basis for Taiwan and European partners to share insights and engage in joint efforts to uphold the free, open, and rules-based international order.

Later on the same day, Deputy Minister Wu, Deputy Secretary-General Lin, and Lieutenant General Hsieh took the stage to speak about Taiwan’s policy approaches and practices in confronting complex security threats and in safeguarding peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait from the perspectives of diplomacy, whole-of-society resilience, and national defense.

The three of them were interviewed by BSC Chairman Reinhard Wolski and took part in a Q&A session. Deputy Minister Wu emphasized that Taiwan has never been a part of China. He further noted that Taiwan and Europe share fundamental values and vital interests, and that closer cooperation would be mutually beneficial. Taiwan would continue to strengthen its self-defense capabilities and whole-of-society resilience, enhance partnerships with like-minded countries, and build a network of partners capable of deterring coercion from escalating into aggression.

Deputy Secretary-General Lin then shared Taiwan’s experience in promoting whole-of-society resilience to counter complex threats. Lastly, Lieutenant General Hsieh elaborated on Taiwan’s achievements in elevating national self-defense capabilities.

For the first time, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs organized a delegation from Taiwan’s drone industry to participate in the BSC defense industry exhibition, forming another highlight of Taiwan’s participation in this year’s conference. Four Taiwanese companies sent representatives to the exhibition to showcase Taiwan’s drone-related products and technologies, namely, Thunder Tiger, Hsuan Yuan Tech., 7A Drones, and Taiwan Drone 100. They attracted considerable attention from government agencies, enterprises, and research institutions, as well as media outlets. The event provided Europe’s security and defense community with a closer look at Taiwan’s achievements in developing the drone industry and building secure and trusted supply chains.

The BSC is one of Europe’s most prominent forums on security and defense policy. Each year, it brings together government officials, parliamentarians, military leaders, industry representatives, think tanks, scholars, and experts from Europe and other regions, giving them the opportunity to exchange views on issues related to European and global security, defense policy, and emerging technologies.

Taiwan’s involvement in this year’s BSC spanned such fields as diplomacy, national security, defense, industry, think tanks, and youth engagement. In terms of the level of participation, the breadth of issues addressed, and the substantive nature of exchanges conducted, Taiwan had a greater presence at the conference compared to previous years. This further enhanced Taiwan’s visibility within the global security community and advanced several policy objectives regarding Taiwan-Europe security cooperation, drone industry diplomacy, and youth participation in international affairs. （E）
